questions.q: The mean of five numbers is $24$. When a sixth number is added, the mean becomes $26$. What is the sixth number?
questions.answer: Sum of 5 numbers $= 5 \times 24 = 120$. Sum of 6 numbers $= 6 \times 26 = 156$. Sixth number $= 156 - 120 = 36$.

questions.q: What is the median of the data set: $\{14, 8, 22, 19, 11, 25, 17, 30\}$?
questions.answer: Sort in ascending order: $8, 11, 14, 17, 19, 22, 25, 30$. The two middle numbers are $17$ and $19$. Median $= \frac{17 + 19}{2} = 18$.

questions.q: An outlier is defined as any data point greater than $Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$. If $Q_1 = 20$ and $Q_3 = 35$, which value is considered an outlier?
Exam scores are normally distributed with $\mu = 75$ and $\sigma = 6$. What percentage of scores fall between $69$ and $81$?
questions.answer: The interval $69$ to $81$ represents $\mu \pm 1\sigma$ ($75 - 6$ to $75 + 6$). By the Empirical Rule, this contains approximately $68\%$ of the distribution.

questions.q: If a test score of $88$ has a $z$-score of $2.5$ with standard deviation $\sigma = 4$, what is the mean score $\mu$?
Which change will increase the standard deviation of a dataset?
choices: Subtracting the mean from each data point
questions.answer: Multiplying by $2$ doubles the dispersion and doubles the standard deviation. Adding/subtracting a constant shifts the data without affecting standard deviation.

questions.q: A fair six-sided die is rolled twice. What is the probability that both rolls result in a prime number?
questions.answer: Prime numbers on a die are $\{2, 3, 5\}$ (3 out of 6, probability $\frac{1}{2}$). For two independent rolls: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.q: If $P(A) = 0.5$, $P(B) = 0.6$, and $P(A \cup B) = 0.8$, what is $P(A \cap B)$?
questions.answer: $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) \Rightarrow 0.8 = 0.5 + 0.6 - P(A \cap B) \Rightarrow P(A \cap B) = 1.1 - 0.8 = 0.3$.

questions.q: A box contains $5$ red balls and $7$ black balls. Two balls are drawn in succession without replacement. What is the probability that both balls are red?
questions.answer: Probability of first red $= \frac{5}{12}$. Probability of second red $= \frac{4}{11}$. Combined probability $= \frac{5}{12} \times \frac{4}{11} = \frac{5}{33}$.

questions.q: How many distinct $3$-person executive committees (President, Vice-President, Treasurer) can be elected from a club of $10$ members?
questions.answer: Since roles are distinct, order matters (permutation): $P(10, 3) = 10 \times 9 \times 8 = 720$.

questions.q: How many subsets of $3$ elements can be formed from a set of $8$ elements?
In how many ways can $4$ math books and $3$ science books be arranged on a shelf if all math books must be grouped together and all science books must be grouped together?
questions.answer: There are $2!$ ways to arrange the two subject groups. Math books can be permuted in $4! = 24$ ways, and science books in $3! = 6$ ways. Total $= 2 \times 24 \times 6 = 288$.
